clue.text: Amuse with gossip about a couple from Vermont

indicators.note: the gossip goes about, that is around, the other piece
a couple means just two letters, taken from the start of the place name

explanation.surface: Someone entertains friends with juicy tittle-tattle about a pair from Vermont.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone is to entertain them, taking their mind off serious matters.

clue.text: Break up group after girl has son

indicators.note: after places the group second, behind the girl and her son

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A pop group splits after one member becomes a mother of a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband is to dissolve an organisation, so its members break up.

clue.text: Bad habit involving duck, say

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like a zero

explanation.surface: A bad habit that involves a duck, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the usual 'for example' tag on duck; it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to say it, putting it into words.

clue.text: Morally justifiable to gain influence over German conservative

parts.note: to win someone over is to gain their support

explanation.surface: A justification for trying to sway a German Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-wing describes the conservative side of politics, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Confused birds trapped in pit

indicators.note: something trapped in a place sits inside it, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: pit is slang for one's bed

explanation.surface: Some bewildered birds find themselves stuck down a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests a hole in the ground, but here it is the informal word for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means puzzled or bewildered, a straightforward synonym of confused.

clue.text: Bird bath oddly filled by one bird

indicators.note: something filled by another holds it inside
oddly means the odd-numbered letters are kept

explanation.surface: A birdbath oddly occupied by a single bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like wading bird known for its booming call.

clue.text: Turing practised it at home in the middle of Bloomsbury

indicators.note: a piece placed in another sits inside it
the middle of a word is its central pair of letters, here the outer piece

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for home

explanation.surface: Alan Turing pursued his work at his home in central Bloomsbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Turing was the British mathematician who helped crack the Enigma code.
explanation.definitionFit: Turing was a mathematician, so mathematics is the discipline he practised.

clue.text: Butcher left hare's gut in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is a disorderly jumble, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A butcher leaves the hare's innards in an untidy heap.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher looks like the noun for the shopkeeper; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to kill brutally or in large numbers, which is what slaughter means.

clue.text: Give in exhausted in the centre of Saratoga? Just the opposite

indicators.note: reverses the stated placing, so the second piece goes inside the first instead

parts.note: done in or done means worn out

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Someone gives up, worn out, in the middle of Saratoga Springs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the clue puts the tired word inside the middle letters; 'just the opposite' swaps that so the middle letters go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, especially money to a cause.

clue.text: Toilet's in shed, I hear

indicators.note: what I hear is a sound, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a rider who is shed by a horse has been thrown

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the lavatory is in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like the garden hut; it is the past tense of the verb, as when a horse sheds its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Throne is jocular slang for the lavatory seat.

clue.text: Tosses stolen weapon

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a weapon they had nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult made of a forked stick and elastic band is a simple projectile weapon.

clue.text: Two ton wagon

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for ton
a wain is an old farm wagon

explanation.surface: A wagon that carries a load of two tons.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an archaic word for the number two, as in 'never the twain shall meet'.

clue.text: Turn away right after Cameron loses his head

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: David Cameron, former UK Prime Minister, known as Dave

explanation.surface: A politician turns away from the right after being decapitated, politically speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron here is the former Prime Minister David Cameron, often called Dave.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert your eyes is to turn them away from something.

clue.text: Mistake relating to quote on the radio

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning

indicators.note: what is on the radio is heard rather than read, so go by its sound

explanation.surface: A broadcaster makes an error with a quotation on air.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an error caused by failing to notice something.

clue.text: Undeterred by discharge in river

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
spit is discharge from the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone carries on regardless of the effluent pouring into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite means in spite of, so not put off or held back by something.

clue.text: Drink leads to ruin amongst wayward Wrens

indicators.note: something amongst others sits in their midst
wayward means wandering astray, so these letters stray from their order

parts.note: to undo someone is to ruin them

explanation.surface: Alcohol brings disgrace to some unruly women of the naval service.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrens were members of the Women's Royal Naval Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset.

clue.text: A delicacy from somewhere in France — extremely tasty

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters are kept

explanation.surface: A French regional food speciality that is very tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes delicacy a tasty food; it is used in its other sense of fine detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a subtle detail or fine distinction, which is what delicacy can also mean.

clue.text: At a disadvantage after split caused by repressive measures

parts.note: being down means losing or behind

explanation.surface: A faction is left weaker after a schism brought about by harsh policies.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a severe set of measures taken to suppress something.

clue.text: Riddle's strange meaning Niobe initially ignored

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
an ignored letter is left out of the word
initially points to the first letter of the name, the one to drop

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A puzzle in Greek myth whose odd significance Niobe failed to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzling question or mystery, the same as a riddle.

clue.text: Kindly Welshman needing no introduction at island retreat

indicators.note: without its introduction, the first letter is gone

parts.note: Taff is a traditional nickname for a Welshman

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: A friendly, famous Welshman holidays at an island hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Taff, from the River Taff in Cardiff, is a slang nickname for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and easy to talk to, which is what kindly suggests.

clue.text: Spurs' back facing severe criticism over altercation with winger

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
turned over, so the word reads the other way

parts.note: a rap is a sharp rebuke
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A Tottenham defender is harshly criticised after a scuffle with a wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur football club, and winger seems to be a wide footballer; it is a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger here is anything with wings, so a small common bird fits.

clue.text: Bad-tempered around Earl without a doubt

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, surrounding it

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is certainly irritable company.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb meaning certainly, without any doubt.

clue.text: Section in party meeting resistance after triumph in House

indicators.note: after sends the party section second, behind the triumph
one piece placed in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: A faction within a party faces opposition after winning in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: House looks like Parliament; it is the royal house, the family name of the British monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is the name of the British royal house, a dynasty in the sense of a family line.

clue.text: Consumes drink after exercise

indicators.note: after sends the drink second, behind the exercise

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to exhaust or finish it, the same as consuming it.

clue.text: Engaged in fixing Ken's roof with a piece of PVC

indicators.note: fixing a roof means working on it and rearranging its parts
a piece here is a single letter, the first one

explanation.surface: Someone is busy repairing Ken's roof using a bit of plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken for describes someone already promised to another, as an engaged person is.

clue.text: Port upset over Immanuel's head girl

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards
the port's letters are split and laid over the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Acre is an ancient port in Israel

indicators.note: the head of a name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A port city is turned upside down by a philosopher's leading young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name, a feminine form of Eric.

clue.text: A passage from Habakkuk or another sacred book

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch of text, so the letters run straight through these words

parts.note: spans the end of the prophet's name and the next two words

explanation.surface: A reading taken from the Book of Habakkuk or some other scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Habakkuk is a book of the Old Testament, so the surface stays among scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koran is the holy scripture of Islam, so it is a sacred book.

clue.text: Get as far as edge of box leaving gap in defence

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word is taken out of it

parts.note: a breach is a gap in a wall or defences

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A footballer gets to the edge of the penalty box through a hole in the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, getting all the way there.

clue.text: Mount pictures at last in oddly neglected cabin

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word
neglecting the odd letters leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone finally hangs pictures in a strangely abandoned hut.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount looks like the verb for putting up pictures; it is a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Run into old fellow packing soothers for Boots

indicators.note: one letter goes into the following pair, sitting among them
packing something means holding it inside

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Al, a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A runner collides with an elderly man who is carrying ointments for footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots looks like the chemist chain, fitting soothers; it is the footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmorals are laced ankle boots, named after the Scottish royal residence.

clue.text: Spread through most of country reaching Delaware after Virginia

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it except the final letter
after places the Delaware abbreviation behind the Virginia one

explanation.surface: Something spreads across a nation, reaching Delaware after Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervade is to permeate, diffusing throughout every part of something.

clue.text: Provider of security for worried monarch lacking bit of muscle

indicators.note: a worried mind is disturbed, so the letters are thrown into disorder
lacking means without, so one letter is dropped
a bit of the word is just its opening letter, the one removed

explanation.surface: A fretful king lacking strength looks for someone to keep him safe.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor holds a vessel fast, and figuratively it is a source of stability and safety.
